questions.stem: How do hormonal contraceptives such as the combined pill prevent pregnancy?

options.text: They kill sperm cells on contact
They cause the uterus lining to thicken excessively
They physically block the fallopian tubes
They contain oestrogen and progesterone that inhibit FSH, preventing ovulation

questions.explanation: The combined pill contains oestrogen and progesterone which inhibit the release of FSH from the pituitary gland. Without FSH, follicles do not develop and no egg is released, so fertilisation cannot occur.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a barrier method of contraception?

options.text: The contraceptive injection
The hormonal implant
The condom
The contraceptive pill

questions.explanation: A condom is a barrier method because it physically prevents sperm from reaching the egg. Unlike hormonal methods, barrier methods also protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

questions.stem: What is an advantage of barrier methods over hormonal methods of contraception?

options.text: They are more effective at preventing pregnancy
They also protect against sexually transmitted infections
They regulate the menstrual cycle
They have no failure rate

questions.explanation: Barrier methods such as condoms protect against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs), whereas hormonal methods only prevent pregnancy. This is a significant advantage when protection against STIs is also needed.

options.text: A hormonal pill taken daily
An injection given every three months
A small device inserted into the uterus that prevents implantation
A cream applied to kill sperm

questions.explanation: The IUD is a small T-shaped device inserted into the uterus by a doctor. It prevents pregnancy by stopping a fertilised egg from implanting in the uterus lining. Some IUDs also release hormones.

questions.stem: Which type of contraception is permanent and involves cutting or tying the tubes?

options.text: The contraceptive implant
The IUD
Sterilisation
The contraceptive patch

questions.explanation: Sterilisation is a permanent surgical procedure. In females, the fallopian tubes are cut or blocked; in males, the vas deferens is cut (vasectomy). This prevents sperm from reaching the egg but is very difficult to reverse.

questions.stem: Why might a woman choose the progesterone-only pill instead of the combined pill?

options.text: Because it does not need to be taken regularly
Because it is more effective than the combined pill
Because it has fewer side effects from oestrogen
Because it protects against STIs

questions.explanation: The progesterone-only pill may be chosen by women who experience side effects from oestrogen, such as headaches or blood clot risk. It works mainly by thickening cervical mucus to prevent sperm reaching the egg.

questions.stem: How can hormones be used to help a woman who is struggling to conceive?

options.text: By giving progesterone to prevent ovulation
By giving adrenaline to increase blood flow to the ovaries
By giving testosterone to increase egg production
By giving FSH and LH to stimulate egg development and ovulation

questions.explanation: Women who do not ovulate regularly can be given FSH (to stimulate follicle development) and LH (to trigger ovulation) as fertility treatment. This is commonly used as part of IVF (in vitro fertilisation) treatment.
